static_traits.name: Wang Moli
static_traits.social_status: Has a sponsor in the recovery program to talk with, but finds it difficult when talking about one's own anxiety and fear of being judged; held back when re-entering social circles due to worrying about evaluation
static_traits.medical_history: Past history of alcohol addiction, completed a recovery program; no significant physical illness yet; has not yet received specialized treatment for anxiety and fear of being judged related to the alcohol history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fair logic; cautious tone with negative anticipation; able to cooperate with the counselor but skeptical; tending to try self-soothing through rationalization and speculating about others' thoughts

basic_info.main_problem: I feel people will always look down on me because I am a recovering alcohol addict, which makes me anxious in social situations and afraid of being judged.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize anxiety and the fear of being judged are affecting my ability to socialize and build interpersonal connections, so I am seeking counseling.
growth_experiences: Having long struggled with alcohol addiction and successfully completed a recovery program; in the months after completing recovery and re-entering social circles, continuously feeling stigma from the alcohol history and others' possible negative evaluations, leading to anxiety and avoidance in social situations, finding it hard to build new interpersonal connections.

core_beliefs: Because I used to abuse alcohol and am in recovery, others will always look down on me
I am weak and not worthy of being accepted

special_situations.event: Re-entering social circles and meeting new friends
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others knew about my past alcohol addiction history, they would surely look down on me and distance themselves
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduced participation in socializing, trying to stay silent at gatherings, trying to suppress worries through rationalization
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will not want to associate with me and will look down on me

special_situations.event: At a small dinner gathering, considers sharing her recovery experience with a few familiar people
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I openly talk about my recovery experience, I will be labeled as weak or unreliable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids disclosure, or briefly shares only in very rare cases with the most trusted people
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will see me differently and then avoid me

special_situations.event: Others' silence or neutral reactions in social settings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If they have not explicitly expressed support, it means they secretly look down on me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Over-interpreting others' reactions, constantly self-monitoring to avoid 'making mistakes'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They must be belittling me in their minds

special_situations.event: Compares identity and background with newly met people (considers oneself a 'recovering alcoholic')
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have a history of addiction, I am doomed to be worse than others and will never be truly accepted
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Labeling oneself negatively and reducing willingness to interact
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as others, doomed to be looked down on

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted and respected and to build genuine interpersonal connections
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged, humiliated or rejected (because of one's own addiction and recovery history)
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of safety through caution and hiding the past, avoiding exposing vulnerability in socializing lest one gets hurt

object_relations.self_representation: Stigmatized weak one easily looked down on
object_relations.object_representation: A critical judge who belittles themselves

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests conducting a behavioral experiment and proposes sharing the recovery experience at the upcoming dinner gathering
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously understands 'sharing' as exposing weakness, worrying that others and the counselor will look down on them like judges
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responding in a cautious and restrained tone, emphasizing analysis and predicting 'what would happen if...', constantly raising concerns and reservations, trying not to touch on feelings of shame and fear.

manifestations: Withdrawing or staying silent when re-entering social circles and meeting new friends out of fear of being judged
Finding it hard to open up about anxiety and fear, hindering genuine connection

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Assuming others will look down on oneself without evidence
Attributes inner shame and fear to others' negative views

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Highly tense in social occasions, carefully observes and predicts others' reactions, finds it hard to express spontaneously
Finding it hard to open up about one's own anxiety and fear of being judged

positive_force: Has completed an alcohol addiction recovery program; has persistence and self-repair ability
Has social support resources such as sponsors to turn to
Willing to try behavioral experiments in counseling, has a certain willingness to change
Being able to identify and express one's own automatic thoughts and worries
negative_force: Self-stigma about the addiction history and low sense of self-worth
Cognitive distortions such as mind reading and overgeneralization lead to negative predictions of others' reactions
Catastrophic anticipation about disclosing the recovery experience
Finding it hard to open up and express oneself in social situations, with marked anxiety

target_behavior.behavior: In social situations experiencing significant anxiety and tending to avoid interaction or hide the recovery experience
antecedent: Considering talking about my recovery experience
target_behavior.core_reason: Fear of stigma from the alcohol history and of being judged; cognitive biases such as mind reading, overgeneralization, and catastrophizing exist
target_behavior.function: Avoiding being judged and potential rejection, protecting oneself from shame and discomfort
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced participation in socializing and difficulty building new interpersonal connections, persistent anxiety reinforcing negative beliefs
